subject: Wrong seat, sir: the sign says Nvidia, and your chair is on the far right
alt: Nala Ponnappa's cartoon: on a pale yellow ground, three dark chairs stand behind a desk. In front of the desk are three yellow nameplates - 'CHINA' at the left, 'NVIDIA' in the middle and 'USA' at the right. In the middle chair sits Donald Trump, pink-faced, white-bearded and in orange, his brows drawn down and his mouth set. Behind him, at the right, stands a thin man in glasses, a white shirt and a blue tie; he points a finger toward the 'NVIDIA' nameplate and says: 'YOU'RE ON THE WRONG SEAT SIR! THE SIGN DOES NOT READ 'INDIA'! YOUR CHAIR IS ON THE FAR RIGHT!' The same words are hand-lettered across the top. At the lower right is written 'PONNAPPA thefederal.com'.
chutki: Three chairs, three nameplates - China, Nvidia, USA. Trump sits in the middle chair and the official standing behind him corrects him: 'You're on the wrong seat sir! The sign does not read 'India'! Your chair is on the far right!'

The needle is in two places. One, at the world's new table a chip company has a chair between China and the United States - Nvidia now has a name like a country's. Two, the difference between 'Nvidia' and 'India' is not only a few letters; the man who cannot read the name right is sent to his real place, on the far right - which is where he sits in politics too.
